newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league and League Cup final (kick-off times 1400 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
League Cup final
Leicester City v Middlesbrough, Wembley (Sunday, 1400 GMT)

Middlesbrough start as favourites despite their lowly premier league position and see the return of their foreign legion from international duty for the first major cup final in their 121-year history. Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli looks set to return after missing the last two games with a hamstring injury while midfielder Robbie Mustoe is hoping to recover from a hamstring injury for the final. Defender Phil Stamp is out with a knee injury.

Leicester will make their second trip to Wembley in two seasons after a goal in the final minute of extra-time against Crystal Palace last May earned them their place in the premier league. Their last cup appearance under the famous twin towers was in 1969 when they finished 1-0 runners-up to Manchester City.
Aston Villa (5) v Everton (13)

Aston Villa are hoping to build on their 2-0 win at Blackburn two weeks ago as they push for a European place, but will be without Irish midfielder Andy Townsend and striker Lee Hendrie who are both suspended. Striker Tommy Johnson last week joined Celtic for 2.3 million pounds ($3.8 million).

Everton's veteran defender Dave Watson has taken charge until the end of the season following Joe Royle's resignation last Thursday. Everton, with one win in six league games, could be without England midfielder Nick Barmby (knee), defender Craig Short and goalkeeper Paul Gerrard (groin).
Chelsea (6) v Arsenal (3) (kick-off 1115 GMT)
This is a prestigious fixture between two teams battling for London supremacy -- and a clash between the only foreign coaches in the premier league.

Chelsea's Dutch coach Ruud Gullitt has Welsh striker Mark Hughes, Italian midfielder Roberto Di Matteo and Canadian on-loan goalkeeper Craig Forrest suspended. This should pave the way for Gianluca Vialli to return while French defender Frank LeBouf is doubtful with a thigh injury.

Arsenal's 2-1 defeat by Liverpool effectively ended their title hopes but Frenchman Arsene Wenger's side look certain to qualify for Europe. They are without England midfielder Paul Merson, who is recovering from a hernia operation.
Manchester United (1) v Derby County (14)
Manchester United, with only one league defeat in 19 matches, will be looking for a confidence boosting win before their Champions League semifinal at Borussia Dortmund on Wednesday.
Defender David May returned from England duty with an ankle injury, but is expected to be fit, while David Beckham (hamstring), Gary Neville (ankle) and Gary Pallister are doubtful.

Derby won their first game in four outings against Tottenham two weeks ago, and give a debut to Estonian international goalkeeper Mart Poom, signed from Flora last week for 500,000 pounds ($821,000). Croatian captain Igor Stimac (groin) is doubtful, although Irish defender Paul McGrath is expected to be fit after an achilles tendon injury. Defender Lee Carsley is out with a virus.
Newcastle United (4) v Sunderland (16)

England strikers Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand could return for this north-east derby to help stake Newcastle's claim for a European place. Shearer will have a late fitness test after missing the last six weeks following his third groin operation in 10 months while Ferdinand's is hoping his hamstring injury will be fully recovered. New midfield signing Des Hamilton will also have a fitness test and could be added to the squad after his two million pounds ($3.3 million) move from Bradford last week.

Sunderland, with only one win in eight games, are hovering just above the relegation zone but are boosted by the return of Irish striker Niall Quinn to the substitutes bench after seven months out with a knee injury. Striker Alan Johnston, signed for 500,000 pounds ($821,000) from French side Rennes, could make his debut, but defender Andy Melville is out for the rest of the season with an Achilles injury while striker Alex Rae is suspended.
Nottingham Forest (18) v Southampton (20)

Nottingham Forest player-coach Stuart Pearce has a fully fit squad to pick from for this relegation battle. Welsh international goalkeeper Mark Crossley will play despite back and hernia problems, while midfielder Chris Bart-Williams (knee) and striker Kevin Campbell (hamstring) have resumed training.
Southampton, without a win in their last five league games, are desperate for points to get off the foot of the table. Coach Graeme Souness will be without suspended Dutch defender Ken Monkou.
Tottenham Hotspur (10) v Wimbledon (8)

Tottenham Hotspur lost 4-2 at Derby two weeks ago which severely damaged their hopes of a European place and coach Gerry Francis faces mounting worries as he tries to rekindle his side's slight chances. Midfielders David Howells (back ligaments) and Darren Anderton (hamstring) are out while striker Teddy Sheringham is hopeful of playing though he has not trained since suffering double vision in England's England 2-0 friendly win against Mexico at Wembley.

Wimbledon go into the second of the London derbies having not won in the league for over a month, and will be looking for a victory before next weekend's F.A. Cup semifinal with Chelsea. Coach Joe Kinnear has no injury problems.
Liverpool (2) v Coventry City (19) (Sunday, 1400 GMT)

Title-chasing Liverpool entertain struggling Coventry before concentrating on their Cup Winner's Cup semifinal at Paris Saint-Germain on Thursday. Coach Roy Evans will be without defender Mark Wright who serves a one-match ban. Striker Lee Jones has joined Tranmere on loan.

Coventry suffered a blow to their relegation fight when they were beaten by fellow-strugglers West Ham 3-1 two weeks ago. They will be without midfielder Paul Telfer and defender Brian Burrows who are suspended. Midfielder John Salako will undergo an operation on his troublesome knee which has severly hindered his appearances in Coventry's relegation battle.
Leeds United (9) v Blackburn Rovers (12) (Monday, 1900 GMT)

Leeds will be without Ghanaian striker Tony Yeboah and South African defender Lucas Radebe who are away on international duty, but could give debuts to new signings striker Derek Lilley and midfielder Pierre Laurent. Defender Robert Molenaar and midfielder Carlton Palmer are both suspended.

Blackburn coach Tony Parkes will make a late team selection after key members of his squad return from international duty, including Scottish heroes Kevin Gallagher and Colin Hendry who celebrated a 2-0 win over Austria.
